description:
Field Recording of people on a frozen lake in Germany.

Children are playing and laughing, some people are ice-skating and an ice hockey game of sorts is taking place in some distance. There's a small dog barking from time to time and the sound of a bus driving by along a lone road far away at one point.

name: frozen lake
description: A field-recording taken standing next to a frozen lake. There is no snow on the lake and the sun is warm, so what you are hearing is the ice slowly cracking all over the lake and reverberating through the water/ice. There is also wind present and I am not good enough to remove it in a good way, so I leave this sound entirely as was recorded.

name: winter-fun ice-skating NL 0113 PM 170122_1082
description:
People, jong and old, skating on the natural ice of a small water called ‘Kloosterwiel’ near the city of Zaltbommel in the Netherlands.
About the pictureThe photo shows a frozen lake in a winter landscape, with several individuals skating across the ice and others seated on a sled. In the foreground, a microphone is mounted on a stand at the edge of the lake. It is intended for recording ambient sounds, likely capturing the cracking of the ice, the movement of the skaters, and other environmental noises. The ice near the shore is broken into large shards, while further out it is solid enough to support safe skating and sledding. Leafless trees are visible in the background, indicating a winter setting. Bright sunlight reflects off the ice, contributing to a calm and clear atmosphere.
About the environment and recording The ice is about 6-8cm (2-3 inches) thick. Recorded on >20meters. Water edge is on 2 meters, so sometime you hear the water coming from under the ice onto the sandy shore. Behind the microphones the river-dike and the busy river Waal which you can not hear. History of the Kloosterwiel The Kloosterwiel (Monastic Wheel) arose because the Waal River broke through a levee. This happened even before dikes were in the Bommelerwaard (the area). Such a levee break is called a crevasse and forms an elongated, shallow pond. At the Kloosterwiel is this still be seen well. Kloosterwiel probably originated in the tenth century, at least before the dikes that were built in the Bommelerwaard between the tenth and eleventh centuries. The wheel was formerly known as St. Peter's Wheel. The wheel water level rises and falls with the river, the influence of the river Waal is keenly felt here. The hiking trails are now part of the higher and drier seepage dams. Haunting monks According to legend, here on the site of the Kloosterwiel there was a monastery. The story goes that monks wandered the old strict rules of discipline and diligence. Excess, drunkenness and lust were introduced in the monastery. As punishment the river Waal began to swirl and fizz and engulfed the monastery with its inhabitants. Instead, there is now the Monasterywheel (OK, not really, the monastery is located next to the wheel, lying on the spot where vegetable gardens). But fore a long time been resurrected monks at night, dressed in white robes, passersby to withdraw the wheel. Local residents therefore never came here after sunset. Accidentally freesound passers, you have been warned now!! Remember the coordinates of the wheel on the map; 51.81038 5.23177 . More here today / More wintersounds Netherlands Date/time: January 22nd Sunday 2017, start 1:13 pm Weather: 2c, clear sunny sky, wind NW 0-1bft, 1026 hPa. Mic pointed S Location; Kloosterwiel, Gamersedijk, Zaltbommel, Gelderland, Netherlands (Holland), Europe, geotag; 51.81038 5.23177 Gear chain: Sennheiser mkh30/50 MS, in Rycote cyclone small, windjammer > Sound Devices 302 >Tascam dr-100 Mk2. name: Rocket Sled Crash On A Frozen Lake In Wisconsin
description: This was an attempt at the ice speed record by a rocket powered snow machine called the Arctic Arrow.  The old record was 247 mph.  On this run he goes 241mph but at the finish line he loses control and crashes quite dramatically!  The driver, Kurt Anderson walked away.  I have photos of the crash as well if interested. This clip is NSFW due to some language at the end, but it really took our breaths away as he was careening thru the snow on frozen Bear Lake in Manawa Wisconsin.  Enjoy!

name: click and sound ice blocks-2.wav
description:
The lake 'Bagsværd Sø' was frozen in February 2021. When the ice broke, the blocks and flakes were blown together on the edge of the lake. A very particular clicking, clinging, and ringing sound occurred. 
The recordings were made by a Zoom H4 with stereo microphone and double wind screen (foam screen plus a woolen sock), still some wind noise appears. The recordings were made in night, to avoid sound from people and traffic.
The recordings have been filtered (Cubase) with a bass cut and a slight lift above 1 kHz.

The recordings have been filtered (Cubase) with a bass cut and a slight lift above 1 kHz.
